transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

I guess mostly I’m just… exhausted. Like not normal tired, but tired in a way that sleep doesn’t really fix. I’ll look at the dishwasher and it feels like this huge project, which sounds ridiculous because it’s just plates and cups. And I’ve been trying to read for this certificate class, and sometimes even that feels like too much, even though I used to be able to sit with stuff like that.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

I don’t know if I’d call it depressed exactly. I mean, I’ve felt… kind of low, I guess, but then I start thinking maybe it’s just because everything piles up, like the mail on the counter, and then I feel stupid for letting it get that way. My sister always says I overthink words like “depressed,” so I’m not sure what counts.
Have you been enjoying things less than you usually do?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I used to have these things that made me feel like me—sketching, or going to gallery openings, cooking something kind of complicated, yoga, even tennis with my friend. And lately I just… don’t care that much. Like I’ll think about doing it and then it feels pointless or like too much effort.  

I actually have a sketchbook sitting out on the table, which normally would bother me in a good way, like it would pull me in, but now it’s just sitting there under some receipts. So… yeah, less enjoyment, I guess.
Have you been feeling hopeless lately?

Hopeless… I’m not totally sure. I don’t sit around thinking, like, “nothing will ever get better,” exactly. It’s more like I get stuck in the weeds of everything, if that makes sense. Like I’ll see the stack of mail and remember I was supposed to call about some bill, and then somehow I’m thinking about how my aunt used to keep every receipt in shoeboxes, which was honestly kind of impressive, but also stressful.

So… I don’t know. Maybe not hopeless exactly. Just kind of worn down.
Did these symptoms start after a specific stressful event or major change in your life?

I guess… yeah, kind of. It wasn’t like one big dramatic thing happened, like someone died or we moved or something. It’s more that around four months ago, the arguments with my spouse started happening a lot more. Like, not even always about huge things—sometimes it’s dishes or a text message, and then somehow it turns into this whole thing.

And I think that’s when this pattern started, around then. Four months or so. Although time has felt a little blurry, honestly, because I keep meaning to mark things on the calendar and then I don’t.
Have you been feeling especially anxious or worried a lot lately?

Um… anxious? I don’t know if I’d call it that. I mean, I worry about things, sure, but then sometimes I’m not sure if it’s “worry” or just me overthinking because there’s too much clutter in my head.

Like yesterday I was staring at the sink because there was this one mug with tea stains, and I started thinking about whether those lemon cleaning videos actually work, and then I forgot why I’d even gone into the kitchen. So… I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed feeling especially anxious in a clear way.
Have these symptoms been making it hard for you to keep up with your responsibilities at work or at home?

Yeah… I think it has, more than I want to admit. I’m not working right now, but I’ve been trying to do this certificate coursework, and I keep falling behind. I’ll make a plan, like “today I’ll do two lessons and pay that bill,” and then somehow the day gets eaten by, I don’t know, reorganizing one drawer or looking up whether you can freeze soup in glass jars, and then nothing important is actually done.

At home it’s been messy. Bills pile up, meals don’t really get planned, laundry and dishes and all that just sort of… stack. My spouse has been having to step in more, which I feel bad about, because they already have enough going on.

And I’ve kind of pulled back from friends and from art things I usually care about. Like I had this little art commitment I was excited for, and now even answering messages about it feels hard to keep track of. So yes, I guess it is making responsibilities harder.
How has your sleep been lately?

Sleep… I’m not totally sure how to answer that. It kind of depends on the night, I think. I haven’t really been tracking it, even though I did download one of those sleep apps once, but then it kept asking permissions and I got annoyed and deleted it.

I mean, some nights I go to bed and then I’m thinking about random stuff, like whether I left laundry in the washer or if I should change the sheets, and then I don’t know how long I’m awake. But I don’t have a clear number of hours for you. It’s been… not very organized, I guess.
Have you felt this low-energy and less-interested way most days for at least two weeks?

Yeah… yes, definitely more than two weeks. I was trying to think when it started, because time has been kind of slippery, like I’ll think something was last week and it was actually a month ago.

But this quieter, heavy kind of stretch—where I’m tired and just not that interested in things—has been going on maybe about three months now. It’s not dramatic every single day, but most days, yeah, it’s been there.
How has your appetite been lately?

It’s been kind of off. Like, I don’t always feel hungry, or I’ll mean to eat and then suddenly it’s late and I realize I’ve had coffee and maybe a few bites of something all day.

Which is weird because I used to be more of a snack person, like I’d always have crackers or leftovers or something around. I even bought those containers for meal prep and they’re just sitting there taking up space. But, yeah… my jeans have been looser lately, and I’m not trying to lose weight or anything.
Have you been feeling worthless lately?

Worthless… I don’t know if I’d use that exact word. I mean, sometimes I feel like I’m not doing much, but then I get stuck thinking about what “doing much” even means, because people are always posting all these productive morning routines and color-coded calendars and it makes me feel behind.

But worthless, like completely? I’m not sure. I haven’t really thought of it that way.
Have you had any thoughts that life isn’t worth living, or thoughts of hurting yourself?

Um… I’m not sure how to answer that exactly. Like, I’ve had those moments where I’m just exhausted and everything feels kind of pointless, but I don’t know if that’s the same as thinking life isn’t worth living.

And “hurting myself” sounds very… specific, I guess. I haven’t really sat down and made some clear thought out of it. It’s more like my brain goes quiet or blank, and then I end up scrolling through random videos about organizing pantries or people renovating old houses, which is weird because I don’t even own a house.

So… I don’t know. I don’t think I have anything clear like that to tell you.
Have you had thoughts that you would be better off dead?

I don’t know… “better off dead” feels like such a heavy phrase. I don’t think I’ve had it in that exact way.

Sometimes I just get tired of thinking, if that makes sense, like I want everything to pause for a while. But then my mind jumps to stupid stuff, like whether I forgot laundry in the washer or if I should finally clean out the fridge. So I’m not sure if that counts. I don’t really have a clear yes-or-no answer.
Before this period started, have you ever had another time in your life when you felt this same kind of low mood and loss of interest for at least two weeks?

I’m not really sure. Like, I’ve had times where I felt down before, but I don’t know if it was this same thing or if it lasted two full weeks. I don’t really track it that way.

I remember in college I had a stretch where I stopped caring about classes for a while, but then again I also hated my schedule and the cafeteria was weirdly depressing, so I don’t know if that counts. It’s hard for me to separate “low mood” from just… life being annoying or me getting stuck in a rut.

So I guess I don’t have a clear answer. I’d have to think about it more.
Would you say the problems with your spouse are the main reason these symptoms started?

I mean… maybe? It’s hard to say it’s the main reason, because once things start feeling bad, everything sort of gets tangled together.

But the timing does line up. This whole pattern has been going on for, I guess, about four months now, and it started around when my spouse and I started arguing a lot more. Like not just little bickering about dishes or whatever—though honestly dishes somehow become a whole thing—but more frequent arguments in general.

So I don’t know if I’d say they’re the only reason, but yeah, that’s around when it started.
Before this started, was there ever another time in your life when you felt low and lost interest in things nearly every day for at least two weeks?

I’m honestly not sure. I know you asked that before, and I’m trying to think of it the right way, but my memory of those periods is kind of blurry.

I’ve definitely had times where I was in a funk or didn’t feel like doing much, but “nearly every day for at least two weeks” is hard for me to pin down. I don’t usually mark it on a calendar or anything. Like, I can remember random details from those times—what apartment I was in, or some dumb thing I was watching—but not whether it was every day or how long it lasted exactly.

So… I can’t really say yes. I just don’t know.
If the arguments with your spouse were not happening, do you think you would still be feeling this same low-energy, less-interested way?

I don’t know. I want to say yes or no, but it’s not that clean in my head.

Like, if the arguments weren’t happening, maybe I’d have more space to feel normal, I guess? But then sometimes I wonder if I’d still feel kind of flat anyway and just find something else to focus on. It’s hard to separate it out because when you live with someone, it’s not like you can put that whole part of your life in a separate box.

And honestly, even small things can set the tone for the whole day—like if the morning starts tense, then I’ll notice everything more, like the laundry sitting there or the weird silence in the kitchen. So… I’m not sure. I can’t really tell what I’d be like without that going on.
Do these symptoms feel stronger than you would expect just from the arguments with your spouse?

I’m not totally sure how to judge that. Like, stronger than I’d expect… I don’t know what the normal amount is supposed to be, you know?

Arguments can really throw me off, especially when they keep happening, but then sometimes I’ll think, well, lots of people argue and they still manage to go about their day. And then I start comparing myself to, like, my sister or people I know, which probably isn’t helpful because everyone acts fine from the outside anyway.

So… maybe? But I can’t really say clearly that it’s more than I’d expect just from the arguments. It’s hard for me to measure.
On days when things are relatively calm with your spouse, do you still feel this same low-energy, less-interested way?

Yeah, I think so. I mean… even on days when nothing big happens and it’s not tense at home, I’m still just tired in this heavy way.

Like, I’ll look at the dishwasher and think, okay, that’s not a big deal, that’s five minutes, but it feels like this whole project. Or I’ll try to read for my certificate class, and my brain just kind of goes, no, absolutely not. And then I’ll end up doing something pointless instead, like reorganizing the pens in a drawer, which sounds ridiculous when I say it out loud.

So yes, I guess the low-energy part is still there even when things are calmer. Sleep doesn’t really seem to reset it.
At any time before this current period, was there ever a stretch of at least two weeks when you felt down or lost interest in things nearly every day?

I’m not sure. I mean, I’ve had times before where I was in a funk, but pinning it down to “two weeks” and “nearly every day” is hard for me.

I don’t really track things that neatly. Like, I’ll think back and remember a month as being bad, but then I don’t know if it was actually every day or if I’m just remembering the worst parts. And time gets weird in my head—like last winter feels like it was three years ago and also yesterday, if that makes sense.

So… I can’t honestly say yes. I don’t have a clear stretch in mind where I’m like, yes, that was definitely at least two weeks nearly every day.

doctor.intent: Determine whether this is a recurrent depressive episode by clarifying any prior episode of similar depressive symptoms before the current one.
doctor.question: Before this started, was there ever another time in your life when you felt low and lost interest in things nearly every day for at least two weeks?

target_item.reason: The question asks about a prior lifetime episode of low mood and loss of interest lasting at least two weeks before the current period, but the symptom profile only describes current symptoms and duration, not past depressive episodes.

patient.answer:
I’m honestly not sure. I know you asked that before, and I’m trying to think of it the right way, but my memory of those periods is kind of blurry.

I’ve definitely had times where I was in a funk or didn’t feel like doing much, but “nearly every day for at least two weeks” is hard for me to pin down. I don’t usually mark it on a calendar or anything. Like, I can remember random details from those times—what apartment I was in, or some dumb thing I was watching—but not whether it was every day or how long it lasted exactly.

So… I can’t really say yes. I just don’t know.

doctor.intent: Clarify whether the depressive syndrome is independent of the marital stressor, which helps distinguish major depressive disorder from adjustment disorder with depressed mood.
doctor.question: If the arguments with your spouse were not happening, do you think you would still be feeling this same low-energy, less-interested way?

target_item.reason: The question is asking about whether the symptoms are caused by or dependent on the spouse arguments, which is an etiological/counterfactual issue not covered by the symptom profile items.

patient.answer:
I don’t know. I want to say yes or no, but it’s not that clean in my head.

Like, if the arguments weren’t happening, maybe I’d have more space to feel normal, I guess? But then sometimes I wonder if I’d still feel kind of flat anyway and just find something else to focus on. It’s hard to separate it out because when you live with someone, it’s not like you can put that whole part of your life in a separate box.

And honestly, even small things can set the tone for the whole day—like if the morning starts tense, then I’ll notice everything more, like the laundry sitting there or the weird silence in the kitchen. So… I’m not sure. I can’t really tell what I’d be like without that going on.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the current depressive symptoms are clearly in excess of what would be expected from the marital stressor, helping distinguish major depressive disorder from adjustment disorder.
doctor.question: Do these symptoms feel stronger than you would expect just from the arguments with your spouse?

target_item.reason: The question asks whether the overall symptom severity feels disproportionate to the spouse-related stressor, which is about attribution/context rather than any specific symptom profile item listed.

patient.answer:
I’m not totally sure how to judge that. Like, stronger than I’d expect… I don’t know what the normal amount is supposed to be, you know?

Arguments can really throw me off, especially when they keep happening, but then sometimes I’ll think, well, lots of people argue and they still manage to go about their day. And then I start comparing myself to, like, my sister or people I know, which probably isn’t helpful because everyone acts fine from the outside anyway.

So… maybe? But I can’t really say clearly that it’s more than I’d expect just from the arguments. It’s hard for me to measure.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the symptoms persist independent of the marital stressor, which best distinguishes a major depressive episode from adjustment disorder at this point.
doctor.question: On days when things are relatively calm with your spouse, do you still feel this same low-energy, less-interested way?

target_item.name: Fatigue
target_item.manifestation: Mostly I’m here because I’m tired in a way that sleep doesn’t fix, like even unloading the dishwasher or reading for my certificate class can feel like too much.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the low-energy feeling persists even when spouse-related stress is calmer; although they also mention less interest, the most direct focus is the ongoing fatigue/low energy.

patient.answer:
Yeah, I think so. I mean… even on days when nothing big happens and it’s not tense at home, I’m still just tired in this heavy way.

Like, I’ll look at the dishwasher and think, okay, that’s not a big deal, that’s five minutes, but it feels like this whole project. Or I’ll try to read for my certificate class, and my brain just kind of goes, no, absolutely not. And then I’ll end up doing something pointless instead, like reorganizing the pens in a drawer, which sounds ridiculous when I say it out loud.

So yes, I guess the low-energy part is still there even when things are calmer. Sleep doesn’t really seem to reset it.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there has been a prior major depressive episode, which best distinguishes recurrent major depressive disorder from a single episode and from adjustment disorder.
doctor.question: At any time before this current period, was there ever a stretch of at least two weeks when you felt down or lost interest in things nearly every day?

target_item.reason: The question asks about whether there was a prior two-week depressive stretch before the current period, but the profile only describes the current depressive symptoms and does not include past episode history.

patient.answer:
I’m not sure. I mean, I’ve had times before where I was in a funk, but pinning it down to “two weeks” and “nearly every day” is hard for me.

I don’t really track things that neatly. Like, I’ll think back and remember a month as being bad, but then I don’t know if it was actually every day or if I’m just remembering the worst parts. And time gets weird in my head—like last winter feels like it was three years ago and also yesterday, if that makes sense.

So… I can’t honestly say yes. I don’t have a clear stretch in mind where I’m like, yes, that was definitely at least two weeks nearly every day.

opening_question.intent: Learn the patient's main reason for seeking care today
opening_question.question: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a current depressive episode lasting about 3 months with low energy/fatigue, markedly reduced interest/pleasure, low mood, impaired concentration/productivity, decreased appetite with likely weight loss, and clear functional impairment at home/socially/coursework. Although symptoms began around marital conflict, they persist even on calm days and meet threshold for a depressive episode; prior distinct episodes were not established, so recurrent depressive disorder is not supported.
